dataChanges.description: Fresh imported records persist canonical priority explicitly in existing YAML formats. No schema migration is required. Selected legacy records missing priority can receive an audited priority-only update after preview and raw-snapshot CAS; existing supplied priorities are not overwritten.

architecture.decision: Place shared evidence normalization and bounded repair helpers in planfile/sync/priority.py. Preserve whether an explicit priority was supplied through TicketState, its builder, GenericBackend conversion and operations extraction; retain malformed evidence until the shared boundary can issue a concrete diagnostic. Normalize selected fresh imports before constructing persistent records or recording sync success, and validate previews through the same boundary. Canonical values are critical, high, normal and low; equivalent evidence agrees after normalization, while contradictory supplied evidence fails closed. Existing-ticket updates retain local priority. Repair helpers accept explicit ticket selection, inspect raw records rather than default-filled models, preview proposed changes, and apply only missing-priority changes through the existing locked store update with raw snapshot CAS and normal audit metadata. Local admission currently reports no active implementation tickets or registered scope blockers; historical issue278 orchestration is preserved and ownership must be reobserved before any future allocation.
interfaceChanges: Add backward-compatible explicit-priority evidence transport to TicketState and BasePMBackend.build_ticket_state; omitted priority remains distinguishable from a supplied value.
architecture.rollback: Revert the scoped implementation through the normal protected process. Preserve canonical priorities already persisted. Any separately authorized reversal of an applied repair uses a fresh store observation and audited CAS update; never restore stale YAML wholesale or rewrite audit history.

nonGoals: Change Monag validation, fleet admission, lifecycle semantics or scheduling policy.
Run repairs against real local or external backlogs during this planning task.
Add a CLI command, dependency, repository, governance migration or implementation file outside the frozen scope.
Introduce inbound priority-change authority for existing tickets.
Access credentials, initiate external coordination or perform destructive cleanup.
delivery.outcome: Deliver semcod/planfile#278 within the six frozen application paths: canonical persisted inbound priorities, concrete diagnostics, regression evidence and a selected legacy repair preview/application boundary. Subsequent publication follows the existing protected native process; this planning response allocates nothing and performs no edits, commits, repairs or publication.

validation.evidence: Before/after synthetic reproduction records identify both issue references and demonstrate the omitted raw field and labeled-high mismatch without modifying operational data.
Parameterized normalization cases cover all supported label formats, aliases, canonical values, equivalent evidence and the documented default.
Legacy/V1, typed YAML and sharded fixtures assert explicit priority presence in physical YAML and matching fresh typed readback.

Mocked GenericBackend, dictionary and typed transport cases preserve evidence; conflict and malformed-value cases assert concrete diagnostics and absence of rejected-record persistence or successful mappings, including previews.
Existing-ticket and duplicate-identity cases prove local priority survives remote explicit priorities, changed labels and absent evidence.

Selected repair fixtures verify a write-free preview, raw missing-field detection, locked CAS application, stale-snapshot rejection, audit preservation, lifecycle/execution/lease invariance, idempotence and zero remote publication calls.
